title: Amazon OpenSearch Service Pricing: A 2026 Guide
summary: Amazon OpenSearch Service pricing combines four models: On-Demand, Reserved capacity, Serverless, and free tier. Know them to control costs.
body_markdown:
## Activepieces spend alerts for an OpenSearch domain


Activepieces doesn't replace OpenSearch Service. It carries a cost signal from AWS to a named person, so the overrun is caught in the first hour rather than on the invoice.


Its core is MIT-licensed, so the same flow runs on Activepieces Cloud or on your own servers, which matters if the cost data has to stay inside your own AWS account.


Activepieces is a workflow automation platform, and its role here is narrow: receive an event, add context, and deliver it where someone will act.


Its pricing page lists 1 credit per flow run, any number of steps, where Zapier's pricing page bills per task and Make's per module.


So the webhook, the tag lookup, the spend pull and the Slack post below cost one credit together, and the Free plan includes 1,000 credits a month with unlimited flows.


### Alarm to Slack with an owner


When an AWS Budgets threshold or a CloudWatch alarm fires, Activepieces receives it through a webhook trigger. The workflow looks up the domain's owner tag, pulls current and projected spend, and posts one Slack message.


Each alert is one run and one credit, so the Free plan's 1,000 monthly credits cover 1,000 of them.


*(diagram)*


Without the owner, an alert is noise that everyone sees and nobody owns. With it, the replica setting, the storage growth or the idle capacity gets a question put to the one team that created it.


If a domain has no owner tag, the workflow can say so in the message, which is itself a finding worth acting on.


Instead of, or alongside, the Slack post, Activepieces can open a ticket, so the alert has a trail that survives a scrolled-away chat. The destination can be chosen from the 750 integrations counted in its open source monorepo.


### Daily cost digest from Cost Explorer


Once a day, a scheduled flow queries Cost Explorer, filters to the OpenSearch domain's tags, and posts a short summary: yesterday's spend, the month so far, and the projection.


Because the digest arrives every day, a slow climb from growing storage or added replicas shows up as a trend long before it crosses a budget line. Budget alarms catch the jump; the digest catches the drift.


Be clear about the limits. Cost Explorer data isn't instant, so the digest describes yesterday, not this minute.


> Budget alarms catch the jump; the digest catches the drift.


The workflow reports spend and doesn't reduce it; it won't delete an index or shrink a cluster. It also adds a second system to run, with its own credentials and upkeep, so the same hour-one discipline applies to it.


If all you need is a cap, AWS Budgets actions can apply a response on their own, and email or SNS notifications cover a small team. Add Activepieces when the missing integration is routing: an owner, a ticket and a daily habit.


The Free plan is $0 with no card needed, so trying that costs nothing.
